To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the directivity degradation of a coupler due to calibration errors can be expressed in a simple way by means of the directivity of the ideal device (D) and of the ideal calibration standard (S), and that the directivity of a coupler with a given fabrication tolerance can be predicted with reasonable accuracy using a simple formula that relates it to the ideal directivity and to the tolerance.

(i) for the investigated coupler design, a directivity of 20 dB is obtained in the frequency range of 5 to 7 GHz; (ii) this directivity is limited by measurement uncertainties to 18 dB; (iii) fabrication tolerances degrade this value further to 17 dB.

the directivity degradation of couplers due to fabrication toler-ances is not negligible, that the directivity loss due to measurement errors is small compared to the loss due to fabrication errors, and that both effects are well within the accuracy of modern network analyzers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how accurate a high-directivity coupler has to be in order to provide the expected performance.
the question: how accurately can the directivity of high-directivity couplers be determined?
the following questions: How accurately should the calibration of a network analyzer be carried out in order to obtain reliable directivity results?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fabrication tolerances are the main limiting factor in the directivity of high directivity microstrip coupler, and that the calibration errors are of minor significance in most cases.
the directivity is not a parameter which should be measured on a single device, but rather on a set of devices with a certain statistical distribution of the parameters.
the fabrication tolerances are the most critical factor limiting the directivity performance of a microstrip coupler.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
measurement errors are the dominant cause of directivity degradation in couplers designed for directivities in the 20-30 dB range.
, for the investigated coupler design, fabrication tolerances limit the achievable directivity to 30 dB, while calibration errors limit it to 20 dB.
measurement errors can explain most of the discrepancies between the theoretical and measured coupler directivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the directivity of a high-directivity coupler is not a fixed number but a statistical quantity, and that the directivity degradation caused by fabrication uncertainties is much smaller than the degradation due to measurement uncertainties.
fabrication tolerances have a much stronger impact on the achievable directivity than calibration errors.
, in order to obtain a reliable measurement of the coupler directivities, a careful calibration procedure is mandatory.
